report_name: Cloudflare Fixes Container Cross-Tenant Data Exposure Flaw

vulnerabilities.name: Cloudflare Containers Cross-Tenant Data Exposure
vulnerabilities.description: A misconfiguration in the Linux device mapper thin provisioning (`dm-thin`) layer, where the `skip_block_zeroing` option was enabled, could have allowed a tenant to read residual data from other tenants' containers on the same physical host. A malicious actor could write a small amount of data to a newly allocated 64 KiB block and then read the entire block, potentially accessing up to 60 KiB of stale data from a previous container.

identities.name: Cloudflare
identities.description: Provider of the Cloudflare Containers and Sandboxes services which were affected by a cross-tenant data exposure vulnerability.

identities.name: Oren Yomtov
identities.description: The security researcher who discovered and reported the data exposure vulnerability to Cloudflare.

indicators.name: Linux Device Mapper Thin Provisioning Insecure Configuration
indicators.pattern:
title: Linux Device Mapper Thin Provisioning Insecure Configuration
id: 9c5b1a3d-8e4f-4b2a-9c1d-6f8e7d4c3b2a
status: experimental
description: |
  Detects checks for the 'skip_block_zeroing' parameter in the Linux device mapper thin provisioning module. This could indicate an audit or reconnaissance for a data exposure vulnerability.
  When enabled ('Y' or '1'), this setting prevents the kernel from zeroing out deallocated storage blocks, potentially leading to cross-tenant data leaks in virtualized environments.
references:
  - https://www.infoq.com/news/2026/10/cloudflare-cross-tenant-exposure/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-05
tags:
  - attack.t1592
level: low
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/cat'
      - '/grep'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/sys/module/dm_thin_pool/parameters/skip_block_zeroing'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects attempts to read the configuration of the 'skip_block_zeroing' parameter in the Linux kernel, which was the root cause of the Cloudflare data exposure vulnerability.
